newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's Dainong Group to sell some affiliates.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's Dainong Group to sell some affiliates.

text.p: The Dainong Group, one of South Korea's leading retailing and textile business groups, said on Monday it would spin off eight to nine affiliates in a self-rescue effort by the end of 1998.
The group aimed to raise 640 billion won from the sell-off and additional sales of assets.
"We plan to sell up to nine companies, including unlisted Midopa Food System Co and Midopa Tour and Services Co," said Chun Byung-sam, the group's spokesman.
Dainong's major creditor, SEOULBANK, said the group had 1.84 trillion won in debts as of the end of 1996, compared to total assets of 1.79 trillion won.
"Our fund flows had been disrupted by a sudden takeover for Midopa Department Store," Chun said.
He was referring to the hostile takeover bid in March by Shindongbang Corp, which fizzled out after another large shareholder of Midopa turned against Shindongbang.
Dainong officials said the group had been forced to concentrate resources on defending against the takeover.
